issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named Rideable with method messageOnRide(), but the solution implements and supplies an interface named Mountable which Pig and Seal implement. This name/type mismatch (Rideable vs Mountable) will confuse students and lead to compilation/type errors when following the problem description or using the provided template code that references Rideable.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Either rename Mountable to Rideable in the solution (and ensure it declares String messageOnRide()), and update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable; or update the problem statement and template to consistently use Mountable. Preferably, implement Rideable as specified in the problem statement so the template, tests, and instructions align.

issues.description: The solution repository contains a Rideable.java file that is empty / has no Rideable interface definition, while the problem statement and template expect a Rideable interface with method messageOnRide(). The missing/empty Rideable type in the solution creates a structural mismatch and will confuse students about which interface to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a proper Rideable interface implementation in the solution repository (e.g., public interface Rideable { String messageOnRide(); }) or remove the empty Rideable.java and ensure the intended interface (Rideable) is defined and used consistently by Pig and Seal. This will align solution, template, and problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to the interface as 'Rideable', but the solution implementation introduces an interface named 'Mountable' (and leaves Rideable.java empty). This is the same conceptual entity (animals that can be ridden) given two different identifiers across artifacts, which will confuse students mapping the requirement (use Rideable) to the provided solution code and template Main usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier: rename the solution's 'Mountable' interface to 'Rideable' (update its file name and interface declaration) and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable. Remove or implement the empty Rideable.java accordingly so the interface name matches the problem statement and template.
